question: What three main disciplines are combined in nursing informatics?

options.B: Nursing science, computer science, and information science
options.C: Public health, statistics, and clinical psychology

explanation: Nursing informatics is defined by the integration of nursing science with computer and information sciences to manage healthcare data. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why are hospitals moving from paper ledgers to digital health records?

options.A: To completely eliminate the need for nurses to write narrative notes
options.B: To ensure that patients never have access to their medical history
options.C: To make hospital storage rooms larger and more spacious
options.D: To capture structured data that improves patient care and continuity

explanation: You've got this! Digital systems make it way easier to share clean, organized data so the whole healthcare team stays on the same page. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h1)

question: What is the main feature that makes an Electronic Health Record (EHR) unique?

options.A: It can only be viewed by the specific nurse who typed the notes
options.B: It is stored strictly on a single physical computer in a clinic
options.C: It replaces the need for doctors to diagnose patients
options.D: It shares information across multiple healthcare organizations

explanation: Think of an EHR as a team player—its superpower is letting different hospitals and clinics share patient info seamlessly. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h2)

question: How does real-time data access in an EHR help protect patients?

options.A: By ensuring that patients stay admitted in the hospital much longer
options.B: By preventing any member of the public from viewing health records
options.C: By automatically prescribing medications without a doctor's review
options.D: By reducing medical errors through complete and updated histories

explanation: Having instant access to accurate medication lists and past diagnoses helps clinicians avoid dangerous drug interactions and treatment mistakes. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is the main limitation of an Electronic Medical Record (EMR) compared to an EHR?

options.A: It is usually restricted to a single facility or clinic
options.B: It cannot be viewed by registered nurses or doctors
options.C: It only contains billing information and insurance forms
options.D: It is always written on paper rather than typed digitally

explanation: Good job! An EMR is great for one specific clinic's digital files, but it doesn't easily share that info with outside hospitals. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h3)

question: A patient moves to another city and visits a new hospital network. Which system is designed to seamlessly transfer their complete medical history to the new care team?
explanation: EHRs are built specifically for interoperability, allowing patient data to follow them across different healthcare networks and providers. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the job of clinical decision support tools inside an EHR system?

options.A: To print physical paper charts for doctors to sign
options.B: To trigger automated alerts for drug allergies or abnormal labs
options.C: To calculate the monthly salary of hospital nursing staff
options.D: To automatically discharge patients when they feel better

explanation: You nailed it. These tools act like a smart safety net, popping up with alerts if a lab value is critical or if there's a potential drug allergy. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why is an audit trail an important feature in modern EHR systems?

options.A: It blocks patients from viewing their own laboratory tests
options.B: It tracks every user who opens or modifies a patient file
options.C: It calculates the exact cost of medical supplies used daily
options.D: It replaces the need for nurses to give verbal shift reports

explanation: Correct! Audit trails keep everyone accountable by logging exactly who viewed or changed a patient's chart. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h4)

question: How do EHR systems directly help stop medication mistakes in the hospital?

options.A: By ensuring that medications are stored at room temperature
options.B: By eliminating medication errors caused by poor handwriting
options.C: By stopping doctors from ever prescribing dangerous drugs
options.D: By allowing robots to swallow pills on behalf of the patient

explanation: No more guessing what a messy prescription says! Typed digital orders take away the danger of misreading doctor's handwriting. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h5)

question: A nurse needs to check a patient's lab results from three days ago during an emergency. What is the primary operational advantage of using an EHR in this situation?

options.A: Automatic notification sent to the hospital director
options.B: Instant retrieval of past records without searching physical files
options.C: Immediate permission to discharge the patient home
options.D: Free medical insurance coverage for the laboratory test

explanation: Digital archiving allows clinicians to pull up historical lab data in seconds, supporting faster and safer emergency decisions. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following is a major infrastructure barrier to EHR implementation in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Frequent power outages and unstable internet connectivity
options.B: Laws that strictly forbid the use of computers in medicine
options.C: Excessive availability of free software for every clinic
options.D: A complete lack of sick patients needing documentation

explanation: Unreliable power supply and poor internet access pose significant daily challenges to maintaining continuous digital health records in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h6)

question: Why can resistance from experienced staff make it hard to introduce EHR systems?

options.A: Staff accustomed to manual filing may struggle or refuse to adopt new workflows
options.B: New software systems require staff to have engineering degrees
options.C: Experienced nurses refuse to administer medications through digital orders
options.D: Older clinicians automatically delete all hospital data upon logging in

explanation: Change is tough! People who are used to paper charts can find it stressful to learn a brand new digital way of working. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h6)

question: What security practice involves giving staff access only to the patient files needed for their specific job duties?
explanation: Role-based access limits what parts of an EHR a user can see based on their specific job role, protecting patient privacy. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h7)

question: Why is sharing login passwords with a colleague considered a serious breach of EHR security?

options.A: It automatically deletes all lab results stored in the database
options.B: It compromises accountability and violates patient confidentiality
options.C: It increases the hospital's monthly internet subscription fee
options.D: It causes the computer screen to freeze and crash completely

explanation: Audit trails link actions to specific user accounts; sharing credentials makes it impossible to know who actually accessed or changed a record. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h7)

question: Who represents the primary user group of Electronic Health Record systems in a hospital setting?
explanation: Nurses document the largest share of daily patient care data, making them the primary users of clinical EHR systems. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h8)

question: In what way do nurses act as safety guards when using an EHR system?

options.A: By reviewing computerized alerts and verifying medication orders
options.B: By writing paper security codes on the walls of patient wards
options.C: By restricting doctors from ordering any laboratory tests
options.D: By physically repairing broken computer keyboards and monitors

explanation: Nurses use their clinical judgment alongside system prompts to catch potential errors before they reach the patient. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h8)
